caption: The drawing depicts an ornate metal samovar with intricate designs covering its surface. The object has a domed lid with a pointed finial at the top and relief floral patterns along the sides of the lid and body. Two large, decorated handles with scrollwork extend from either side of the samovar, and the front features an ornate spigot with an elaborate, horizontally-oriented handle. The body of the samovar has a bulging, rounded shape with embossed patterns and a central cartouche containing what appears to be monogrammed letters. The samovar stands on four curved, decorative legs which are attached to a circular base underneath the spigot, most likely intended to hold a small heating element or burner. The entire drawing is rendered in graphite pencil on a plain, lightly textured, beige or off-white paper, creating a monochromatic composition with varying shades of gray to indicate depth, highlights, and shadow. The artist's name, Nicholas Zupa, is written in small letters at the bottom right corner of the drawing.
title: Silver Hot Water Urn
